text:
shreya: heads up — received a DSAR (user request) for full data erasure. user id: u-9001. They explicitly asked to remove any embeddings or derived vectors. ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/PRIV-482

shreya: quick summary of the tricky bit: embeddings are stored in VectraDB (vendor). we use envelope encryption: our CMK = projects/redwood/locations/global/keyRings/emb-kr/cryptoKeys/emb-key. VectraDB keeps daily snapshots for 30 days and says they cannot delete snapshots immediately (their policy).

shreya: also found a problem with our deletion endpoint (/internal/privacy/delete-embeddings) — if the caller omits the proof header we currently return 500 with a stack trace. that could leak internal info. reproduced locally: 
```bash
curl -X POST 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $PRIV_TOKEN" 
  -d '{"user_id":"u-9001"}' 
  https://internal-api.redwood/api/v1/privacy/delete-embeddings
# response: 500 Internal Server Error
# server log: NullPointerException at com.redwood.privacy.DeleteHandler.delete(PrivacyService.java:213)
```

alice-sec: yikes. first priorities: 1) mitigate vuln (don't return stack traces; return 400/401), 2) lock down endpoint so only privacy-runbook service account can call it, 3) get retention-exception path started for vendor snapshots.

alice-sec: for RBAC: we should create a short-lived role for service account privacy-deleter@redwood.gsvc that has kms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter on emb-key and API access to VectraDB deletion endpoint. avoid giving blanket project roles.

tom-infra: confirm re: CMK — emb-key is customer-managed. access currently granted to service accounts: internal-ml, model-serve. changing will require break-glass approval if we remove existing bindings. also rotation could create a key version mismatch with vendor snapshots.

tom-infra: quick commands that helped me inspect key versions: 
```bash
gcloud kms keys versions list 
  --keyring=emb-kr --key=emb-key --location=global 
# shows versions and state (ENABLED/DESTROYED)
```

mike-legal: from legal: we need proof of deletion vs. an admission we requested it. if vendor holds immutable snapshots for 30 days, we need to either get a retention-exception approved or get vendor to promise purge on request (in writing). timeline? 

shreya: vendor initial reply: they can do a scope-reduced deletion (live index) within 24h but snapshots require retention exception. they asked for an authorized API call from our org + KMS proof token.

luis-platform: auditability note — we must emit a structured audit event when delete runs: fields: actor, service_account, user_id, request_id, cmk_key_id, vendor_response_id, deletion_scope (live/index/snapshots), result (started/queued/failed). sample line for redwood-audit: 
```json
{"ts":"2023-10-12T18:43:12Z","actor":"privacy-runbook","svc":"privacy-service","user":"u-9001","req":"req-5a3","cmk":"projects/redwood/locations/global/keyRings/emb-kr/cryptoKeys/emb-key","vendor_id":"vectra-op-348","scope":"live-index","result":"queued"}
```

alice-sec: also need to ensure audit logs are immutable and retained 7+ years for compliance team access. make sure KMS decryption ops are logged in Cloud Audit Logs (dataAccess).

tom-infra: quick note on KMS IAM: granting roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter to privacy-deleter service account is fine for decrypt. if vendor expects a wrapped token we may need to create a signed JWT that proves we hold the key — discuss with Vectra engineering.

shreya: the deletion endpoint bug is highest risk. assigning @alice-sec + @tom-infra to patch: return 4xx on missing proof header, no stack traces, and verify auth. can you triage?

alice-sec: on it. will open a short-lived PR to sanitize errors + add tests. also will add new IAM policy proposal and post a link.

ops-bot: deploy/ci: privacy-service v2.8.6 build passed — staged deploy queued (pipeline #4125).

luis-platform: for retention-exception flow: suggest we create a temporary evidence record that ties the exception approval to the DSAR — store exception id in the audit event and in the ticket. sample: RETEX-2026-022.

mike-legal: please capture vendor email confirming they will delete live index entries within 24h and their backup retention policy. legal needs that to sign off on exception if we go that route.

shreya: next steps (owners): 
- patch deletion endpoint to not leak stack traces & validate proof header (alice-sec)
- prepare RBAC change + least-priv role for privacy-deleter (tom-infra)
- audit event schema + BigQuery ingestion (luis-platform)
- vendor retention exception request + gather signed confirmation (mike-legal + shreya)
- open retention-exception ticket and attach evidence RETEX-2026-022 (shreya)

shreya: ETA: aim to have mitigation (patch + temporary RBAC lock to privacy-runbook only) within 6 hours. retention exception/ vendor confirmation will follow (48-72h).

alice-sec: noted. logging an internal incident for tracking: INC-8972. tagging for postmortem if vendor process caused delay.

shreya: thanks all. updating PRIV-482 with owners. will post updates here as we get vendor proof. :pray:
